note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 27-year-old male presented via telemedicine minutes after a suspected bee/wasp sting to the arm with localized rash and anxiety about breathing/lip swelling; no visible lip/oropharyngeal swelling or respiratory distress on video; managed as localized allergic reaction with OTC antihistamines and emergency precautions.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Insect sting (bee vs wasp unclear) to arm a few minutes prior, with localized redness/rash and puncture mark at the site. Reports feeling anxious, with non-acute “difficulty breathing,” a “weird” sensation of the tongue, and mild soreness with possible right-sided lip swelling.
- Timeline: Sting occurred just minutes before consult. Symptoms stable at time of call; breathing discomfort not “particularly acute.”
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: None reported. No medications taken prior to consult.
- Associated symptoms: Localized rash, blotchy/erythematous area at sting site; patient notes possible mild right lip soreness/swelling; “tongue feels a bit weird.”
- Pertinent negatives: No prior anaphylaxis. No known food or pet allergies. Clinician observed no visible lip swelling and breathing “seems all right” during the call.
- Systems review (limited by telemedicine): No stridor reported or observed. No generalized hives reported. No systemic symptoms reported beyond anxiety.

Past Medical History:
- Eczema (history; no current complications documented).
- Anxiety/panic attacks (occasional; never treated with medication).

Allergies:
- Penicillin.

Medications:
- None reported for this event prior to consult.
- Current routine medications: not documented.

Social History:
- Occupation: Computer scientist.
- Living situation: Lives alone.
- Pets: Cat at home.
- Tobacco/alcohol/illicit drugs: Not discussed.

Family History:
- No relevant family history or history of acute reactions reported.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- General/Respiratory (telemedicine): Clinician noted breathing appears normal; no stridor observed; patient able to converse.
- HEENT (telemedicine): Lips appeared not swollen to clinician. Oropharyngeal view obtained; no visible swelling documented. Patient reports right-sided lip soreness; tongue feels “weird.”
- Skin: Arm sting site with slight redness and blotchy rash; puncture mark visible. No significant local swelling per patient; clinician did not appreciate notable swelling.

Investigations:
- None performed or ordered during this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Localized allergic reaction to insect sting (bee vs wasp) of the arm; low concern for anaphylaxis at time of assessment.
  - Antihistamine recommended:
    - Chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet up to 6 times daily; route not documented.
    - Alternative: once-daily antihistamine (name/dose/route not documented).
  - Safety-netting/return precautions:
    - Seek immediate care in the Emergency Department if breathing difficulty, progressive lip/tongue/throat swelling, stridor, or rapid symptom progression occurs.
    - Contact clinic or seek care if symptoms worsen or new concerns arise.
  - Infection watch: If erythema spreads, area becomes hot, or other signs of local infection develop, clinician advised that antibiotics may be needed (not prescribed at this visit).
  - Education provided: Information link on anaphylaxis; reassurance provided. No allergy testing indicated at this time; consider blood testing if reactions/rashes become recurrent.

- Issue 2: Penicillin allergy.
  - Documented; no antibiotics prescribed today.

- Issue 3: History of anxiety/panic (occasional).
  - Not on medication; reassurance provided; advised low threshold to contact clinic if worrying symptoms or concerns.

General plan items:
- Follow-up as needed if symptoms persist, worsen, or recur.
- No EpiPen prescribed or indicated in this encounter based on current presentation.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; comprehensive medication list/reconciliation; smoking/alcohol/substance use history; detailed ROS; laterality of arm not specified.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Sting site described as “arm,” later referred to by clinician as “wrist” (conflict noted).
  - Insect type uncertain (bee vs wasp).
  - Patient age stated as 27 with DOB 1991-11-17; potential age inconsistency depending on current date (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Some fragmented/incomplete phrases typical of live telemedicine; overall history and plan understandable.
